preconditions.expression: n == int(stdin.split()[0]) and n >= 1 and n <= 2 * 10**5
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 200,000) representing the number of points.
Each of the next n lines contains exactly four integers a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i (1 ≤ a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i ≤ 10^9) representing the coordinates x_i = a_i / b_i and y_i = c_i / d_i.

preconditions.expression: all(b_i != 0 and d_i != 0 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:n+1] for b_i, d_i in [line.split()[1], line.split()[3]])
preconditions.description: Denominators b_i and d_i are non-zero, ensuring x_i and y_i are well-defined.

preconditions.expression: all(a_i > 0 and c_i > 0 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:n+1] for a_i, c_i in [line.split()[0], line.split()[2]])
preconditions.description: Numerators a_i and c_i are positive, ensuring x_i > 0 and y_i > 0.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().splitlines()[0].isdigit() and (c := int(stdout.strip().splitlines()[0])) >= 0 and c <= n // 2
postconditions.description: The first line of output is an integer c (0 ≤ c ≤ n/2) representing the maximum number of moves possible.

postconditions.expression: all(len(move.split()) == 2 and move[0] != move[1] and 1 <= int(move[0]) <= n and 1 <= int(move[1]) <= n for move in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:c+1])
postconditions.description: Each of the next c lines contains two distinct integers a and b (1 ≤ a, b ≤ n, a ≠ b) representing the indices of points removed in a move.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(move[0]) <= n and 1 <= int(move[1]) <= n and int(move[0]) != int(move[1]) for move in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:c+1])
postconditions.description: Each move involves two distinct points that exist at the time of the move.

postconditions.expression: all(set(move) not in {set(move2) for move2 in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:c+1] if move != move2} for move in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:c+1])
postconditions.description: No point is involved in more than one move.

postconditions.expression: all(unique_points := set(range(1, n+1)), all(int(move[0]) in unique_points and int(move[1]) in unique_points for move in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:c+1]), len(unique_points) == n - 2 * c)
postconditions.description: The total number of points removed is exactly 2 * c, and no point is reused across moves.

postconditions.expression: all((a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i := [int(x) for x in stdin.splitlines()[1 + int(move[0]) - 1].split()]), (a_j, b_j, c_j, d_j := [int(x) for x in stdin.splitlines()[1 + int(move[1]) - 1].split()]), (x_a := a_i / b_i, y_a := c_i / d_i, x_b := a_j / b_j, y_b := c_j / d_j), any((x_a_new := x_a + 1, y_a_new := y_a) or (x_a_new := x_a, y_a_new := y_a + 1), (x_b_new := x_b + 1, y_b_new := y_b) or (x_b_new := x_b, y_b_new := y_b + 1)), (x_a_new * y_b_new == x_b_new * y_a_new) for move in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:c+1])
postconditions.description: For each move, there exists a way to move points a and b such that the new coordinates (x_a_new, y_a_new) and (x_b_new, y_b_new) are collinear with (0, 0), i.e., x_a_new * y_b_new == x_b_new * y_a_new.
